data.name: Vishnukant
data.gender_notes: Vishnukant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who protects and preserves the universe. A name inspired by Lord Vishnu, the preserver and protector in Hinduism. The name Vishnukant carries the meaning “Lord Vishnu” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi, Marathi. Parents who choose Vishnukant usually hope their child will grow to embody lord vishnu and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies devotion and faith towards Lord Vishnu, who is believed to protect and preserve the universe.
data.etymology: Vishnukant belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Vishnu.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vishnukant total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_sanskrit.name: विष्ठुकान्त्
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: विष्ठुः (Vishnuh) + कान्त् (Kantah) = God + heart = God in the heart

in_hindi.name: विष्ठुकान्त्
in_hindi.meaning: दिव्य पुरुष के धात्रे विष्ठु वहने रहना
in_hindi.long_meaning: विष्ठु (Vishnuh) + कान्त् (Kantah) = दिव्य पुरुष (Divine Person) + कान्त् (Kantah) = वहने रहना (dwelling in) = God dwelling in a divine person

in_tamil.name: விஷ்ணுகந்த்
in_tamil.long_meaning: விஷ்ணு (Vishnu) + கந்த் (Kanthan) = இந்த (this) + இரத்தில் (in this place) + விஷ்ணுவின் (of Vishnu) + இருக்கும் (is present) = This place where Vishnu is present

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Vishnukant was a renowned Jain scholar of the 12th century AD. The name Vishnukant carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
